title: Vikings Elevate Kyle Van Noy & DeeJay Dallas for 2026 Week 1 Vs. Packers - vikings.com
content: EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings on Saturday announced the elevations of outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and running back DeeJay Dallas ahead of hosting the Packers to open the 2026 regular season. Van Noy and Dallas joined Minnesota's practice squad on Sept. 2 and are poised to make their debuts in Purple on Sunday. Kickoff is 3:25 p.m. (CT) at U.S. Bank Stadium. View Vikings practice photos from September 10 at TCO Performance Center ahead of the Week 1 matchup against the Packers. Van Noy, 35, is entering his 13th NFL season. The 2014 second-round pick of Detroit has started 115 of 173 regular-season games for the Lions, Patriots, Dolphins, Chargers and Ravens. He overlapped with Vikings Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores in New England and Miami, helping the Patriots win Super Bowls LI and LIII. Van Noy has totaled 561 tackles, including 74 for losses and 57 sacks. He has four career interceptions to add to an outside linebackers room led by Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner. Dallas, who will turn 28 on Sept. 16, has appeared in 84 games for the Seahawks, Cardinals, Panthers and Jaguars. He has rushed 124 times for 538 yards and four scores while adding 64 catches for 407 yards and two scores, including one from new Vikings starting QB Kyler Murray in 2024. Dallas also has logged 1,303 special teams snaps during his career. The 2020 fourth-round pick by Seattle has averaged 25.3 yards on 89 kickoff returns and 9.4 yards on 39 punt returns. title: Tanacha Suksot Joins GS Caltex for Growth - 조선일보
content: Aiming to support Silva, embrace leadership, chase championship at new club [OSEN=Son Chan-ik Reporter] “I thought I needed to throw myself into a new environment to develop further.” Choosing change over familiarity, Tanacha Suksot (26), an outside hitter from the Thai national team, embarks on a new challenge wearing the GS Caltex uniform. Tanacha, who took her first steps in the V-League in 2023 with Korea Expressway Corporation, described her time there as “one of the best memories of my life.” Though filled with good memories, she did not want to become complacent. She judged that changing her environment was necessary to grow as a volleyball player. Meeting Tanacha at GS Caltex’s training camp in Japan on the 12th, she stated, “I felt that a change in environment was necessary to develop further as a volleyball player. Throwing myself into unfamiliar situations could be an opportunity to take another step forward in life.” The first club to reach out to Tanacha, who had decided to pursue change, was GS Caltex. She explained her decision to transfer, saying, “When I started considering a transfer, GS Caltex contacted me first. I wanted to join a team that highly valued my abilities.” Coincidentally, the team she faced in last season’s Championship Finals. From the opponent’s court, GS Caltex was a team that was difficult to stop once they gained momentum. Reflecting on it, Tanacha said, “Once they gained momentum, it was really hard to break their flow. The ‘chemistry’ between the players seemed very tight. I could feel their trust in each other even on the court.” Now, she has directly entered that tight-knit environment. There are differences too. Her position within the team has changed. Born in 2000, Tanacha was relatively young at Korea Expressway Corporation, where there were many veterans. At GS Caltex, she has become someone who must lead the younger players. She laughed, saying, “At Korea Expressway Corporation, when we divided into senior and junior teams during training, I was the oldest in the junior team. But here, I’m on the senior side to the point where I can’t show any immaturity.” One of the aspects GS Caltex expects from Tanacha is balance in attack. Until last season, the team’s offense was heavily concentrated on Gisele Silva, who boasts formidable attacking power, having become the first in V-League history to surpass 1,000 points for three consecutive seasons. There are expectations that Tanacha’s addition will reduce Silva’s offensive burden. However, Tanacha shook her head at the expression “I need to lessen Silva’s burden.” “Volleyball is a team sport. When all players participate in the attack, it becomes easier and more fun. Rather than thinking, ‘I need to reduce Silva’s burden,’ I believe it’s important for each player to fulfill their role.” Silva also welcomed the new teammate. After hearing that Tanacha would join GS Caltex, she expressed anticipation, saying, “She’s a player who works hard on defense and has good attacking skills. I think we can play fun volleyball together.” Hearing Silva’s words, Tanacha smiled brightly. “I’m really grateful for those words. It’s very meaningful to me. Becoming a better player together—that’s the image of a volleyball player I aspire to.” The values Tanacha pursues are clear. She considers being remembered as a “good teammate” as important as individual achievements. She said, “I can’t always play well. There are days when things go well and days when my performance doesn’t meet expectations. But being a good teammate is something I can strive for. When I look back on my volleyball career, I hope to be remembered as ‘a good teammate.’” That’s why she believes her role becomes more important when the game doesn’t go as planned. She approaches her teammates first, saying, “It’s okay. Let’s try again,” to lift the atmosphere. This mindset also reflects the unique culture of Thai volleyball. The characteristic of Thai volleyball that Tanacha highlighted is “volleyball that is enjoyed.” She explained, “Even if Thai players make mistakes, they don’t dwell on them too deeply. They smile and quickly move on to the next play. I think this mindset keeps the atmosphere alive and improves performance.” Overcoming physical disadvantages with diverse attacks is also a strength of Thai volleyball. “Since Thai players aren’t generally tall, we use a lot of combinations. Instead of attacking from just one spot, we move inside and outside to add variety to our attacks. I want to showcase this a lot this season.” Off the court, she is also active in building a “good team.” Her love for board games is not just a hobby but a way to get closer to her teammates. Tanacha explained, “If everyone just looks at their phones during free time, there’s no opportunity to talk while facing each other. Playing board games naturally makes us sit across from each other, share stories, and get to know each other better. I believe the closeness and trust built off the court eventually show on the court.” Wearing a new uniform and standing at a new starting line, Tanacha’s goal is clear: winning the championship. Although she experienced the joy of finishing first in the regular league with Korea Expressway Corporation, she did not reach the top of the Championship Finals. She emphasized, “I want to win the championship while doing my best. I will never give up on that goal.” Even in the process of chasing her goal, she doesn’t want to lose her own color. A player who chases the ball until the end and, when the team falters, is the first to smile and reach out to her teammates—that is the image Tanacha is drawing at GS Caltex. “I want to always be a teammate who gives good energy. This season, I’ll smile a lot.” /what@osen.co.kr

title: Candidate aghast at $500Gs bill for 'field with fence' dog park - Toronto Sun
content: A candidate for council says he was told that spending half a million dollars to fence in a dog park is 'just the way it is' at Toronto City Hall See more Toronto Sun on Google — save as a Preferred Source How do you spend half a million dollars fencing in a field? Shawn Allen thinks City Hall has a spending problem, and his first, best example is the new off-leash dog park at Lawrence Ave. E and Starspray Blvd. – east of Port Union Rd.  He wants to be the next city councillor for Scarborough-Rouge Park, and for him the project has been something of a crash course in Toronto politics. “It’s a field with a fence. We’re paying for a fence. That’s what it is,” Allen told the Toronto Sun. “We’re paying to fence in a space – I think it’s 800 square metres, if I’m not mistaken – and we’re paying half a million dollars for that. And the majority of the cost is consulting fees, mobilization fees, arborists, geotechnical engineers, all these things. “Why do we need a geotechnical engineer to put a fence around grass? The dogs were running along the grass perfectly fine before they put up the dog park. Why can’t the dogs run along the grass and just fence it in?” Subscribe now to read the latest news in your city and across Canada. City Hall hasn’t provided an answer for the “why.” While the park was designed with input from residents in Scarborough-Rouge Park ward, the plan never went before committee to be scrutinized by city councillors and the public. The city wouldn’t confirm the project’s $500,000 price when asked by the Sun. The only official number comes from a motion by the incumbent councillor, Neethan Shan, to redirect $200,000 in funding for improvements from a nearby park, the Royal Rouge Tot Lot, to the off-leash area. Allen said he’s confident in the price because of a conversation with the project coordinator. “I said, why does it cost 500,000? She’s like, ha ha, that’s just the way it is. I go, what do you mean that’s just the way it is, ha-ha-ha? “We gotta figure this out. This city’s going broke.” In a statement, City Hall said construction at both the dog park and the Royal Rouge Tot Lot should be complete this fall. A final project cost and name for the dog park are still to come. Your noon-hour look at what's happening in Toronto and beyond. Please try again The city did not address questions about what the redirection of funds means for the Tot Lot, Allen’s conversation with the planning official or why a dog park would need a six-figure budget. Allen said he’s a dog owner and is in favour of off-leash parks – “but I’m just looking at the cost.” “For 500,000, you could house 108 people at $2,200 a month, so what’s the priority?” Shan redirected the Tot Lot funds with a member’s motion during May’s City Council meeting. While councillors can debate such motions, they typically draw little attention and this one passed with a quick show of hands. In an emailed statement, Shan focused less on the off-leash park and more on the Tot Lot improvements, which had a $300,000 budget – but got $530,000 in funding. Shan said he secured money from a playground enhancement program to pay for more amenities, including an accessible picnic table, a fitness pod and more play features. That funding allowed him to send the $200,000, from a pool of what’s known as Section 37 money, to the dog park budget. (While the Sun asked why a dog park would need a half-million-dollar budget, Shan did not address this in his statement.) “The kids didn’t get less money, they got more,” Shan wrote. “We listened to the community, improved the original plan and secured more investment to deliver more for residents.” Shan’s a rookie councillor but a veteran politician. He spent years as a school board trustee in both York Region and Toronto, then briefly served as city councillor for Scarborough-Rouge River, winning a 2017 byelection in what was Ward 42 in the city’s former 44-ward model. The ward map was redrawn, and he narrowly lost to Jennifer McKelvie in 2018’s election. When McKelvie left last year for Parliament, Shan won another byelection, while Allen placed third. The left-wing advocacy group Progress Toronto – founded by Mayor Olivia Chow’s political lieutenant Michal Hay – endorsed Shan last year, hailing him as a “progressive champion.” But Allen said constituents tell him that Shan is hard to get ahold of. He said City Hall is failing to provide Toronto with “value of service.” “The city is a corporation,” Allen said. “We have all these school board trustees as executives on the board of something that they’re not familiar with.” Allen was born and raised in Scarborough, and has run a mortgage brokerage for about two decades. Times are tight for many Torontonians, and Allen thinks City Hall isn’t helping. “We have food bank lines wrapped around the corner in West Hill. People are hungry,” he said. “People have mortgage arrears, people have tax arrears and the mayor’s committed to raising property taxes next year at the rate of inflation. Well, we’re still catching up from the 20% you raised it over the past three years, so now you’re going to put people behind the 8-ball even more … We can’t ask homeowners to find savings when the city’s not doing the same.” Postmedia is committed to maintaining a lively but civil forum for discussion. title: BMW F 450 GS Price Hike: Check New Variant-Wise Prices - Motoroids
content: Months after launching the much-awaited F 450 GS, BMW Motorrad has revised the prices of the ADV in India. Introduced as the brand’s new entry point into the GS family, buyers will now have to spend up to ₹30,000 more depending on the variant. The price hike applies across all three versions, with no new features or mechanical updates included in this revision. The F 450 GS is manufactured in India through BMW Motorrad’s partnership with TVS Motor Company. It replaced the G 310 GS as the brand’s smallest GS adventure motorcycle in the country. The Base and Exclusive versions have received a ₹25,000 price hike, while the top-spec GS Trophy gets the highest increase of ₹30,000. All prices listed below are ex-showroom. The GS Trophy continues as the most expensive version and comes with extra equipment, including BMW’s ERC (Easy Ride Clutch) system. This technology reduces the need to operate the clutch manually during gear shifts. Each variant is offered with a single colour option. The Base and Exclusive variants come in Cosmic Black, while the GS Trophy features Racing Blue with red and white graphics. BMW has left the engine completely unchanged. The F 450 GS continues to be powered by a 420cc, liquid-cooled, parallel-twin engine that produces 47bhp and 43Nm of torque. It is paired with a six-speed gearbox and features a slipper clutch. The use of a twin-cylinder engine separates the F 450 GS from the older G 310 GS, which relied on a single-cylinder motor. The F 450 GS is built on a tubular steel frame. It features a 43mm KYB upside-down front fork and a KYB rear monoshock, offering 180mm of suspension travel at both ends. The motorcycle rides on a 19-inch front wheel and a 17-inch rear wheel with dual-purpose tyres. The motorcycle has a seat height of 845mm. It provides an upright riding position and built-in wind protection for riders planning longer journeys. A 6.5-inch TFT display comes standard, supporting smartphone connectivity and navigation functions. Road, Rain and Enduro riding modes are offered as standard. The higher variants add Enduro Pro mode and extra electronic equipment. Other features include heated grips and adjustable levers. While the GS Trophy benefits from the ERC system, cruise control is not offered on any variant. The BMW F 450 GS now starts at Rs 4.95 lakh and goes up to Rs 5.60 lakh. Nothing else has been added with the latest price revision, so the higher prices are the only change for buyers.

title: BMW F 450 GS Prices Hiked By Up To Rs 30,000 - autocarindia.com
content: BMW launched the F 450 GS earlier this year as their new entry-level ADV, replacing the long gone G 310 GS in India. At launch, the motorcycle raised eyebrows with its ERC (Easy Ride Clutch) that effectively eliminated the need for using the clutch to shift gears. BMW had mentioned that the launch prices were introductory. Well, now the prices have been increased for all three variants. To recap, the F 450 GS has three variants in India: Base, Exclusive, and GS Trophy. The Exclusive variant offered an up-and-down quickshifter as an extra over the base variant and the GS Trophy variant stepped it up with ERC and adjustability to the USD fork. India still hasn’t gotten the Sport variant that sits between Exclusive and Trophy with just the adjustable suspension. At launch, the Base variant cost Rs 4.70 lakh, the Executive variant cost Rs 4.90 lakh, and the GS Trophy variant cost Rs 5.30 lakh (all prices, ex-showroom, Delhi). With the price increase, the Base variant now costs Rs 4.95 lakh, the Exclusive costs Rs 5.15 lakh, and the GS Trophy costs Rs 5.60 lakh. The base two variants have each received a Rs 25,000 increase and the top GS Trophy has received a Rs 30,000 increase. Other than the price increases, the motorcycle continues as-is with no changes to its mechanicals, or features; which means the same 420cc, twin-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine with 48hp and 43Nm of torque. That also means that there’s only one Cosmic Black colour for the Base and Executive variants. GS Trophy also gets one colour, but a different Racing Blue with red and white accents. On the feature side, ERC is still only on the Trophy variant and heated grips continue to be offered as standard, but cruise control is missing, even as an accessory. title: "My volleyball is 23 points; full power goes to deuce." GS's Silva, who never stops, declares a 'full swing' until the very end - starnewskorea.com

Foreign player Gisele Silva (35), currently undergoing training camp in Hitachinaka City, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan, has expressed her determination for the upcoming season. According to a press release from GS Caltex on the 12th, Silva, who led GS Caltex to a championship last season and swept both the regular league and championship finals MVP awards, compared her career to '23 points' out of a perfect 25-point volleyball set. She said, "If I cannot show the same power as before and have to stay on the bench, I should step aside, but until the moment I score the final point, I want to pour out my current energy and power." Silva has become the first foreign player in V-League history to spend four consecutive seasons with a single club, revealing her deep affection for life in Korea and the team. Last season, despite chronic knee pain during the playoffs, she recorded an attack success rate of 50.63% and led the team to a perfect 6-0 championship run. Silva credited her teammates for the victory and expressed strong confidence in winning again this season. The synergy with Tanatcha Soksot, who joined as a new Asia quota player this season, is also a key expectation. Regarding Tanatcha, whom she faced last season in the championship finals, Silva stated, "She is a player with sharp defense and attack, so we should be able to show great chemistry together." Tanatcha's addition is seen as a tactical card that will help disperse the opponent's focused attention and offensive burden on Silva. title: Thanacha Suksom Balances GS Caltex Attack, Emphasizes Team Effort - 조선일보
content: Thai star joins GS Caltex, prioritizing team chemistry over easing Gisele Silva's offensive burden “I thought I needed to throw myself into a new environment to develop further.” Thanacha Suksom, 26, a Thai national team outside hitter, chose a new challenge this season. After joining the Korea Expressway Corporation in 2023 and competing in the V-League, he described his time with the team as “one of the best memories of my life.” Still, he opted for change. Rather than staying in a familiar setting, he wanted to test himself in a new environment. Meeting Thanacha at GS Caltex’s Japanese training camp on September 12, he said, “I felt that changing my environment was necessary to take my volleyball skills to the next level. I believed that putting myself in unfamiliar situations could be an opportunity to move forward in life.” The first team to reach out was GS Caltex. “When I started considering a transfer, GS Caltex contacted me first,” Thanacha said. “I wanted to join a team that highly valued my abilities.” Coincidentally, GS Caltex was the team he faced in last season’s championship finals. At the time, observing them from the opposing court, he found them a tough opponent with few weaknesses. “Once they gained momentum, it was really hard to break their flow. The ‘chemistry’ among the players seemed incredibly tight. I could feel their trust in each other even on the court.” The biggest change Thanacha feels after switching teams is now being part of the “senior line.” Born in 2000, he was relatively young at Korea Expressway Corporation, where veterans were plentiful. But at GS Caltex, he has become a leader responsible for guiding younger teammates. “At Korea Expressway, I was the oldest in the ‘younger team’ during training splits, but here, I’m firmly on the senior side,” he said with a laugh. One role GS Caltex expects of Thanacha is balancing the team’s offense. Last season, the burden of leading the attack fell heavily on Gisele Silva, who became the first V-League player to score over 1,000 points in three consecutive seasons. However, Thanacha shook his head at the idea of “easing Silva’s burden.” “Volleyball is a team sport. When all players participate in the attack, it becomes easier and more enjoyable. Rather than ‘I must reduce Silva’s load,’ it’s more important for each player to fulfill their role.” Silva also welcomes her new teammate. Upon hearing of Thanacha’s joining, she said, “She works hard on defense and has great attacking skills. I think we can play fun volleyball together.” When relayed Silva’s words, Thanacha smiled and said, “I’m really grateful for that. It means a lot to me. Becoming a better player through collaboration is exactly what I aspire to as a volleyball athlete.” “You can’t always perform well in volleyball. There are days when things go smoothly and days when your skills don’t show. But being a good teammate is something I can strive for. When I look back on my volleyball career, I hope to be remembered as a ‘good teammate.’” That’s why Thanacha’s role becomes clearer when matches don’t go as planned. He is the first to approach his teammates and say, “It’s okay. Let’s try again.” This mindset is also influenced by Thai volleyball culture. Thanacha identified the biggest characteristic of Thai volleyball as “enjoying the game.” “Thai players don’t dwell too deeply on mistakes. They laugh and quickly move on to the next play. I believe this attitude keeps the atmosphere alive and improves performance.” Overcoming physical disadvantages with diverse attacks is another trait of Thai volleyball. “Since Thai players aren’t generally tall, we use a lot of combinations,” he said. “Instead of attacking from one spot, we move inside and outside to add variety to our offense. I want to showcase this style a lot this season.” Off the court, Thanacha also focuses on building a “good team.” His love for board games isn’t just a hobby—it’s a form of “teamwork training” to bond with teammates. “If everyone just stares at their phones during free time, there’s no chance to talk face-to-face. Playing board games naturally brings us together, and through conversation, we get to know each other better. I believe the closeness and trust built off the court eventually show on it.” Thanacha’s goal for this season, in his new uniform, is obviously to win the championship. With Korea Expressway, he tasted the joy of finishing first in the regular league but didn’t reach the championship finals’ summit. “I want to do my best and win the championship. I won’t give up on that goal,” he said. Even while chasing the title, he doesn’t want to lose his unique color. On the court, he chases the ball until the end, and when the team falters, he’s the first to smile and reach out to his teammates. “I want to be a teammate who always gives good energy. This season, I’ll smile a lot.”

title: What a Fed Rate Hike Could Mean for US Stocks - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Investors are pricing in a higher likelihood that the Federal Reserve will hike rates after core CPI inflation rose in August more than economists had estimated. However, a rate hike may not keep the US stock market from climbing higher, says Jonathan Shugar, head of Cross Asset Sales in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities, on The Markets podcast. Companies reported strong earnings growth in the second quarter, and valuations near the 10-year average are not stretched, he explains. Shugar also discusses why a Fed hike may not restrain investment in artificial intelligence, the risks in longer-term interest rates, and the potential opportunity for investors in consumer experience stocks. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Friday, September 11th. Before we start, I want to acknowledge that it's 25 years since the 9/11 attacks. As our chairman and CEO, David Solomon, said in remarks, "Our firm joins the community in honoring the lives lost that day, as well as the first responders, recovery workers, and survivors, and everyone who suffered from 9/11 related illnesses." I'm also joined today on the Goldman Sachs trading floor by John Shugar. John is head of cross-asset sales within FICC and Equities. John, thanks so much for joining us on The Markets. Jonathan Shugar: Thank you for having me, Chris. Great to be here. Chris Hussey: Well, first time, long time for you, I know. Tell us a little bit about cross-asset sales. That could encompass anything. What exactly is it? Jonathan Shugar: What we like to do is be like our clients, which is ultra-flexible as to where the opportunity set is. That's really what drives it. The team is about 25 people, specialists across equities, derivatives, execution, credit, rates, and FX. And so really what we're able to help people do is capture these inflection points in markets, whether that's going from a growth equity cycle to a credit cycle, or whether that is looking at asymmetric hedges. And you've seen the utility of that ever since the subprime crisis to different rate hiking cycles or credit protection, where we look for asymmetric hedges. And we'll talk a little bit more about that later on. Chris Hussey: Yeah. Well, it sounds like having the inflection guy here is perfect because we just got the CPI report. The FOMC meets next week. Looks like we might be in for an inflection. What do you make of the CPI report and the reaction that the market's had so far? Jonathan Shugar: So, I think that the market reaction is telling you that they're going to hike next week. We have something like 84% odds priced for that, and for 50 bps before year-end. That's not to say that inflation has not followed some of what the people who want to hold say, which is you haven't seen shelter inflation continue to go and goods inflation moderated. It was really driven by things like communication services. That being said, with it being so hot and the Fed having said they're data-dependent, the market is telling them that in some ways it's actually more dangerous not to hike because you might lose control of the back end in that case, and that's one of the bigger risks to the market. Chris Hussey: Yeah, it's a great point, cause the Fed controls the front end through their Fed funds rate, but the back end is controlled by the markets, and the markets can do anything they want there. Let's talk a little bit about equities for a second here, because this also is back to school week, and we've had a series of things that always happens in the back to school, and people come back and they're trading heavily. The market, though, has kind of flat-lined since early August. What do you make of the rally that we've had and where do you see it going from here? Jonathan Shugar: So we've had some near-term challenges. Momentum has had an extraordinarily tough last two months. When you look at technical levels here, you have both CTA and systematic flows against you in the near term. That being said, we just finished our Communacopia conference. One of the biggest themes in the market right now is AI. The companies coming out of there could not have been more bullish. And to the people who say the market is expensive, we're trading at a 19 PE. That's the 10-year average. We've had S&P earnings growth of something like 30% on the second quarter. So, if you look at that, you basically have a market where all of the heavy lifting has actually been done on the earnings side. And when you think about the drivers going forward, there's terrific opportunities within various AI consumer sectors which are off highs, to really say that, well, over the next few weeks we may have a lot more speed bumps. But if you and I are sitting here at year-end or we're sitting here next year, we're talking about an S&P that's probably well over 8,000. Chris Hussey: Okay, John, let's examine de-globalization because your customers can invest anywhere in anything all at once, and there have been a lot of geopolitical risks. We're seeing it in the oil tape. What are your customers saying about those geopolitical risks today? Jonathan Shugar: So, one of the most interesting things has been the things that really impacted the market negatively when you think about Liberation Day as the original tariff announcement. Those have become less relevant to price action as we go forward, and it's a trend that we've really seen since COVID, which is the duration of opportunity to take advantage of dislocations to the market is getting less and less, and the moves to correct to the upside are much more violent. Now, when you think about geopolitical risk out there, there's certainly things which are near term. You mentioned oil. If you look at Brent right now, you're trading around 104, but you look out one year, you're buying Brent at, with a seven handle on it. So, this is still viewed as a more near-term problem. That doesn't mean you can't have local disruptions. On the product side, whether it's gasoline, diesel, heating oil, probably looks incrementally worse for Europe than the US, but that can certainly be something that comes up. All of that should be relatively short duration in terms of impact but can certainly drive local price action. When we think more broadly, there are geopolitical impacts on both the positive and negative side. Obviously there's a good reason why you might want to look at a country like Brazil, and we've seen investors increasingly look to buy upside there as they're going into an election in October. Chris Hussey: Brazil. When the market zigs, you zag. I love it. Okay. You're a risk guy. Let's talk a little bit more broadly about risks here because I know you have a view. What are the risks out there that you're watching and how do you wanna hedge them? Jonathan Shugar: So, as we think about what the largest risk on the board is, it really, outside of some of the true tells, which are global geopolitical risk exploding is really in the back end of the rate curve. And that is because, one, there's natural impulse for this to be higher. You have global fiscal deficits. This is not just a US problem. This is everywhere. You have a ton of AI issuance, so hyperscalers doing about $800 billion of CapEx this year. Our analysts estimate something around $1.2 trillion next year. So, there's a lot of natural supply which is competing for money. Now, if you get a really sharp move in rates, cause equities can tolerate higher rates. It's really just the pace of change that has the biggest impact. So, the way we like to hedge that is really in two ways: either buying outright payers or payer spreads on the back end, the 30-year part of the swap curve, or looking out and doing something like a CMS cap, which is the shape of the curve between front and back end, and we think that there's good returns out there. Now, we always love 10 X-type trades. On reasonable strikes, you can probably still make five to six X your premium. And so that's what we're talking to investors about now. Chris Hussey: Five to six X. I thought everything was 10X, but okay. You say equities can tolerate higher rates, but do they tolerate higher rates because as long as the rates are going higher because of inflation, equities are indexed to inflation, so they're a nominal asset, so they go up? What happens if the higher rates are tied to something more like a debasement trade? Jonathan Shugar: So, if they're tied to a true tail risk debasement trade, that would obviously be negative in the short term for equities. If you get true hyperinflation, and you can go back to Zimbabwe or anything you want, that could be really good for equities because they are a nominal asset. That being said, I think the reason people are thinking about all of this is, one, economic growth remains good. The fact is that hiking25 or 50 basis points doesn't change the need for the strongest balance sheet companies in the world to be investing heavily in CapEx, given how transformative a technology AI is going to be, and the consumer outside of the low end still is okay. And so, you compare that to the fact that most consumer stocks are trading 30% plus off their 52-week highs. There just seems a real disconnect here. And so, as you think about equities going forward, people got very surprised by things like biotech performing so well. And biotech, another thing that typically has a lot of correlation negatively to higher end rates being higher. Well, I think consumer and there are pockets of that we like, there are pockets of that we don't like, could be the thing that surprises into your end. By the way, another plug for our conferences, we've got our consumer conference next week. So, we're going to know a lot more after that. Chris Hussey: Okay, you gave us a great hedge trade, but give us one more. What's the trade? Jonathan Shugar: So, I think that there's a lot that can be done here. Number one, within consumer, there's both longs and things that we're more cautious on. On the long side, the experiential type names, whether it's cruise, whether it's events, things that people really want to do and spend money on, especially at the high end, that continues to see a lot of growth. On the flip side, there have been companies releasing agents for consumers. Well, guess what? If you don't have to spend two hours to switch your phone plan to a cheaper plan that's probably something that could be really impactful, and so we're a little bit more cautious on some of the impacts there. We mentioned AI briefly. A lot of the CapEx picks and shovels are trading well below market multiples. A lot of the semis type names trading well below market multiples. You're seeing capital return in some of those places and other interesting things. We think this is a temporary air pocket and those have good runway ahead of them. Chris Hussey: Terrific. Sum us up for this here. What are you watching for next week and the weeks ahead that we should be keeping our eyes on? Jonathan Shugar: So clearly watching the Fed next week, I think that's something where the press conference is going to be a lot more impactful than the actual if they do hike, hike. If they don't hike, that's actually very interesting and may have impact of its own. Outside of that, I think that any clarification on kind of the big picture questions from corporates as you go through the rest of the year on the efficacy of AI in terms of increasing revenue will get people really, really excited again. Outside of that, watching the Giants on Sunday. Hoping that's not another tough season to be a Giants fan. Chris Hussey: J-E-T-S, Jets, Jets, Jets. John Shugar, you're a wealth of information. Thanks so much for joining us. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: “One of the Biggest Statements So Far”: Skatta on Karol G’s “BbY WOW” Global Success - Kaboom Magazine
content: Our latest digital magazine is available for download - CLICK HERE >> “BbY WOW,” which samples the iconic “Coolie Dance Riddim,” gives the classic beat another major global moment. “This beat was different,” Burrell reflects on its enduring impact For years, music producer and industry figure Skatta Burrell has continued to reap the success of his iconic juggling, the Coolie Dance Riddim, as the 2003 production continues to find new life across international music. The compilation, listed by Rolling Stone among the 25 Riddims That Shaped Jamaican Music, became one of dancehall’s biggest international crossovers, powering hits including Elephant Man’s “Jook Gal,” Mr. Vegas’ “Pull Up,” Bounty Killer’s “Yuh Gwan” and more. Its reach stretched even further through Pitbull’s Latin smash “Culo” and Nina Sky’s Billboard Hot 100 Top 10 hit “Move Ya Body,” which was later remixed featuring Vybz Kartel. “The experience of witnessing multiple samples and remixes of the Coolie Dance Riddim is something I’ve been witnessing almost yearly since its release in 2003,” Burrell said, reflecting on the riddim’s longevity. More than two decades later, Coolie Dance continues to move beyond dancehall floors and into the global mainstream. Beyoncé moved to its pulse during her 2023 Renaissance World Tour, while Kehlani sampled the riddim on her 2024 viral hit “After Hours.” Its latest major moment comes through Colombian superstar Karol G, alongside Spanish artistes Judeline and rusowsky, whose “BbY WOW” samples the riddim and climbed to No. 1 on both the Billboard Global 200 and Billboard Global Excl. U.S. charts. The song generated 42.3 million global streams from August 28 to September 3 and has surpassed 116 million streams on Spotify. “This ‘BbY WOW’ hit is by far one of the biggest statements so far, and especially being a Spanish-language song, it seems to be captivating the world due to its infectious melodies and the dynamics and groove from the Coolie Dance beat,” Burrell shared. “No words can explain the gratitude and reassurance I get just knowing I created music that is definitely timeless.” Latin superstar Karol G gives the classic beat another major global moment. For Burrell, the riddim’s continued global success also validates the creative instincts behind a beat that sounded different from much of what surrounded it at the time. “I’ve always known this beat was different and out of the norm, and it reminds me that trying to fit in is never the way to achieving greatness,” he said. “What matters most is the way music makes you feel, and its main purpose is to evoke emotions and movement.” While Burrell admits he never predicted just how far Coolie Dance would travel, he always believed there was more to come from the production. “This global impact was never forecasted. However, I’ve always had that confident assurance inside that there’s always more to come from this Coolie Dance Riddim,” he added. title: Giselle Silva Vows Powerful Finish at '23 Points' - 조선일보
content: Silva leads GS Caltex to title, vows powerful finish despite nearing career's end “If I were to compare my volleyball career to a 25-point set, I think I’ve reached around 23 points.” Giselle Silva, 35, Cuba, who led GS Caltex to last season’s championship and won both the V-League regular season women’s division MVP and the championship match MVP, did not deny that her volleyball career has entered its final stages. However, she said she could not accept the idea of easing up just because she is at “23 points.” Instead, she wants to pour all her strength and energy into the moment she scores the final point. “A professional athlete’s job is physical. If the time comes when I can no longer show the same power as before and have to stay on the bench, I’ll step down. I want to finish my career while still demonstrating the same energy and power as I have now. I must keep showing my relentless drive for victory until the end.” Silva is currently training in Hitachinaka, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan. When met at the Astemo Rivale training facility on September 11, she expressed pride at being the first foreign player in the V-League to spend four seasons with a single team. For Silva, who has traveled across the world playing volleyball, GS Caltex is a special team. She said she never expected to stay in Korea this long when she first arrived. Like before, she could have moved to a new country after one season for another challenge, but after one season in Korea, her perspective changed. Rather than packing her bags again and starting from scratch in a new country, she wanted to stay where both she and her family felt comfortable. Seeing her daughter Ciana, 6 years old, adapt well and enjoy life in Korea only strengthened her desire to remain. Last season, Silva displayed monstrous power by recording a success rate of over 50% (50.63%) in 200 attack attempts during the postseason, leading GS Caltex to a perfect 6-0 championship run. Despite chronic knee pain, she scored over 30 points in six consecutive games, giving the team a valuable trophy. However, she emphasized that the championship was not achieved by her alone. “There were ups and downs, but we found solutions. I’m really proud of my teammates who worked with me to overcome difficulties and achieve the championship. My teammates supported me a lot.” Her faith in the team remains unchanged ahead of the new season. When asked what gives her confidence that they can reclaim the top spot, Silva did not hesitate. “Confidence. We did it last season. Why can’t we do it this season? If every player on the court has that same confidence, I believe we can do it again. Above all, my teammates have grown a lot. I can see it.” This season, Silva has a strong new teammate: Tanacha Suksot, 26, Thailand, who faced her on the opposing side in last season’s championship finals. Suksot, an outside hitter for the Thai national team who played for Korea Expressway Corporation last season, joined GS Caltex as an Asian quota player this season. Silva recalled the intense rivalry with Suksot during last year’s finals, exchanging glances and engaging in fierce battles. When she first heard that her former rival would join the same team, Silva’s first thought was, “This will be fun.” “Tanacha is great at defense and has a fierce attack. Our chemistry will be good, and I think we can show fans exciting volleyball.” Suksot is also a card to reduce the offensive burden on Silva. If Suksot opens up attacking avenues on the opposite side when the opposing defense focuses on Silva, GS Caltex’s offense can become even more diverse. The number most associated with Silva is “1000.” She became the first V-League player to score over 1000 points in three consecutive seasons. While it’s a remarkable record, it also reflects how heavily GS Caltex’s offense has relied on her. “1000 points? I don’t think it’s a perfect situation for the team if I’m the one scoring them. Still, this record holds my pride. It’s a number built by enduring an entire season with strong physical and mental resilience.” GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, “It’s true that Silva shoulders many attacks, but her efficiency is close to 50%, which is high. Making high-probability attacks is the path to victory.” Another pillar supporting Silva’s career is her family. Balancing childcare and her athletic career as a mother who must move around the world is not easy. The person who made this possible is her husband, Luis. “My husband’s life changed 180 degrees. He prioritized my athletic career over his own life so I could continue playing. Without his sacrifice and support, I probably wouldn’t have continued my career until now.” She said her ability to focus entirely on volleyball on the court is thanks to her husband. Asked how she wants to be remembered by V-League fans, Silva’s answer came without hesitation. “I want to be remembered as a player who never gave up and kept fighting until the end.”

title: GS Shop Bets on Lace Trend to Drive Fall Fashion Sales - Seoul Economic Daily
content: Jason Wu Lace Camisoles Draw 120 Million Won in Orders Clothing with lace detailing is drawing attention as "lacecore" emerges as a fall fashion trend. Lacecore applies elements borrowed from lingerie — lace and satin fabrics and slip dresses — to everyday wear. Rather than putting lace front and center, the recent approach layers it under knitwear or jackets as an accent. Fall-winter fashion items with lace detailing are winning strong consumer response at GS Shop, industry sources said on the 12th. Two lace camisole styles, first introduced on the 29th of last month during a broadcast launching Jason Wu's fall-winter line, drew orders for about 2,000 units worth 120 million won. The pieces pair lace trim with softly lustrous satin and feature a diagonal hem, making them easy to layer under jackets or knitwear. La Piaf's new fall-winter "lace detail knit top" also sold more than 1,000 units during a broadcast on the 11th. Morgan's "lace satin skirt," which adds lace at the hem, drew orders for about 2,000 units in its first broadcast. GS Shop plans to air the skirt again on the 12th. Along with responding to the lacecore trend, GS Shop is expanding layering pieces aimed at unpredictable autumn weather, adding garments that can be worn in combination depending on the temperature. Late last month, the company held a "26 FW Fashion Showcase," unveiling a large lineup of fall arrivals from its exclusive fashion brands through its TV home shopping channel and mobile app. For this season, it expanded transitional-weather items such as shirts, blouses, lightweight long-sleeve T-shirts and cardigans, while strengthening pieces that layer well with other garments, including vests and bustiers. The focus was on versatility — items that can be worn alone in early fall and paired with jackets and other outerwear as temperatures drop. One example is La Piaf's "open-up vest and cardigan layered set," which can be styled three ways: the vest alone, the cardigan alone, or the two together. Worn together, the design lets the vest's hem show naturally below the cropped cardigan. Following the ruffled blouses that proved popular last spring and summer, the brand also introduced a "pin-tuck volume blouse" with three-quarter sleeves and pleated detailing. Jason Wu released a fall version of its "Vera Essential Jacket," a summer hit, adding UV protection and quick-drying functions. Core Authentic reinforced its outerwear lines that drew strong customer response last season, broadening its selection with items including the "cupra stadium bomber," noted for its light weight and subtle sheen, along with a hooded field jacket and a high-neck faux-leather blouson. "Order value for our exclusive fashion brands grew about 15.6% year-on-year in the first half, leading growth across the entire fashion category and contributing to earnings improvement," a GS Shop official said. "We have prepared products that can be worn in a variety of ways from the transitional season through winter, so customers don't lose out on newness and style even in unpredictable weather." title: Taylor Townsend, Katerina Siniakova win US Open women's doubles - ESPN
content: NEW YORK -- Taylor Townsend was tight, wasn't moving well and could sense she was swinging her racket early in the US Open women's doubles final. "I wanted this really badly, and I knew that I wanted it," she said. "I felt it in my body and my spirit because I was so nervous." Playing partner Katerina Siniakova talked her through the rough start Friday, and then they found their groove and rolled. Townsend and Siniakova completed their career Grand Slam as a team by defeating the wild-card pair of Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery for their first US Open doubles title together. "It just means the world to me," Townsend said. "This really means everything to me, not only just to be able to win the US Open but to be able to complete a career Slam." It looked dicey early, when Townsend and Siniakova lost the first three games and dropped the first set. At one point, the ball dropped between them, an uncharacteristic mistake for the top two women's doubles players on the planet. Then the top seeds started looking like it with aggressive shots at the net, and they took control of the match on the way to a 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 victory at Arthur Ashe Stadium. "The match was very tight, very tough for us, but we found a way to win it," Siniakova said. "We found a solution. I'm just really happy that we have this one and we can celebrate it together." The result validated Townsend's confidence in her play after getting knocked out in singles by No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka. The 30-year-old American expressed confidence in her tennis at the time, knowing she still had another opportunity in doubles. That turned into her fourth major championship after she and Siniakova won Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and the French Open earlier this year. It was Siniakova's 12th Grand Slam title after winning seven with fellow Czech player Barbora Krejcikova and one with Coco Gauff. "It helps to have someone that's been here so many times and who has been able to get over the hump -- what is it, 12? Twelve times," Townsend said. It was an impressive run for Krueger and Montgomery, who respectively rank 570th and 610th in doubles and went through each half of defending champions Erin Routliffe and Gabriela Dabrowski separately in the quarterfinals and semifinals. Krueger and Montgomery reunited five years after winning the US Open girls' doubles title and advancing a round at the women's level in 2021. "We're both just trying to take it all in," Montgomery said. "What we've just done has been amazing. I think we did forget that we were offered a wild card, so I'm just glad we made good use of it." Townsend and Siniakova, who fell short against Routliffe and Dabrowski in the final a year ago, got a happier result this time. Townsend dropped to her knees after the final point and was all smiles as she said to Siniakova that they finally did it. "If flipping the script had a face," Townsend said, "you'd see my face." A year after famously sipping the tournament's signature cocktail, the Honey Deuce, at the news conference after losing in the women's doubles final, Townsend had one in each hand this time. Carrying just one, Siniakova asked Townsend, "Next year, you have three and I have two?" -- setting the table for the duo to already start thinking about a repeat.

title: How Automation Impacts the Lives and Careers of Displaced Workers - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The rapid advance of artificial intelligence (AI) may have significant repercussions for whole occupations. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that 6%-7% of US workers could be “displaced,” meaning they have to find new employment because their roles have been automated, over the next decade. A look at previous waves of technological automation shows that displacement can have lasting effects on workers, hurting their job prospects and even their chances of starting a family. But past examples of technology-driven unemployment also offer some encouragement: Younger workers tend to find it easier to adjust to replacement, and some are able to cushion the impact on their careers by moving into new fields and retraining, Goldman Sachs Research economists Pierfrancesco Mei, Jessica Rindels, and David Mericle write in a report. How does technological displacement impact a worker’s job prospects? Historically, workers who have been displaced by technology have harder job transitions than those in stable or growing occupations. How does technological displacement affect people’s lives outside of work? The scarring effects of technological displacement extend beyond the job market. Workers displaced early in their careers—between the ages of 25-35—accumulate wealth significantly more slowly than other workers. Even the probability of getting married is lower for workers who were displaced by technology. “A key mechanism driving these worse outcomes is occupational downgrading,” Mei, Rindels, and Mericle write. Technology-displaced workers are more likely to move into occupations with more repetitive, rule-based tasks and lower complexity. That’s likely because the same technological changes that eliminated their positions also eroded the value of their existing skills. How can technology-displaced workers improve their job prospects? The impact of technological displacement varies by worker. In short, generative AI is expected to automate a significant share of work tasks across a range of industries. Many workers will benefit from this change, which will boost their productivity and real income; others will lose their jobs as AI takes over a larger share of their work. “Our analysis suggests that, similarly to previous waves of technological change, AI-driven displacement could impose lasting costs on affected workers, worsening labor market outcomes for several years,” write Mei, Rindels, and Mericle. They add that the effects can be “substantially larger” if workers are displaced during a recession. The research shows that retraining programs could help workers cope with these changes, depending on how AI ripples through the job market. These programs may ultimately enable displaced workers to earn modestly higher wages and achieve more stable employment. Yes—historically, technology-displaced workers take roughly one month longer to find a new job than people in stable or expanding occupations, and they suffer three percentage points higher real earnings losses upon reemployment when moving between full-time positions. A decade after they were first made redundant, technology-displaced workers have lower real earnings compared to comparable workers who lost their jobs in non-disrupted occupations. The likelihood of going through a subsequent spell of unemployment is also higher for technology-displaced workers, particularly in the first five years after they are made redundant. Retraining can make it easier to adjust if your role is automated, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Technology-displaced workers who spent at least four weeks in retraining within three years of their job loss achieve roughly two percentage points more cumulative real wage growth in the next decade compared with their peers who did not retrain. They are also less likely to return to unemployment in that period. Yes—recessions tend to intensify technological displacement, as firms shed more routine jobs during a downturn. title: Karol G’s ‘NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO’ - thecatalystnews.com
content: Making waves across the music charts with her new hit “Bby WOW,” Colombian artist Carolina Giraldo Navarro, known as Karol G, has created a relatively new sound that has fans excited for more. Her new album, “NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO” was released on Aug. 7. Navarro opens the album with an alluring, mechanical entrance track, “Te Llevas To,” which combines electronic sound with a sense of sadness. In a Rolling Stone interview, Navarro described the song as “chaotic.” Staying true to her distinctive voice, Navarro closes the track by creating a sonic contradiction that emphasizes her anger and frustration with the deep bass. The album features Bruno Mars on “Still” and Drake on “Ahí,” two songs with contrasting sounds. “Still” is a sad, rhyming song performed in English, while “Ahí” has a more upbeat sound while expressing similar feelings of love. “Ahí” also contains a catchy form within its song, “Tenlo ahí, tenlo ahí,” translating to “Hold it right there, hold it right there,” which repeats continuously, creating a space for listeners to jam and resonate with her lyrics. The standout is “Bby WOW,” featuring Rusowsky and Judeline. “Bby WOW” explores the complications of loving someone while longing for them. Unresolved relations are the heart of the pre-chorus: “Hoy te vi, las ganas siguen ahí,” which translates to, “I saw you today, the desire is still there.” “When I think of Karol G, I think of perreo,” Beatriz Leiva ‘29 said. Surprisingly to Leiva, this album steers away from perreo, a form of self-expression, celebration and seduction deeply tied to Caribbean and Puerto Rican reggaeton culture. While “NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO” isn’t perreo, it’s something new. Navarro transforms the rollercoaster of her personal life into a vibrant soundscape that celebrates letting go and jamming out.

Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational. On September 8, Reuters reported that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) has opened a new engineering office in Bellevue, Washington, which will house more than 125 employees working on AI and cloud technology. The move gives Goldman a bigger presence in the Pacific Northwest and puts the firm closer to a large pool of technology talent. Goldman already employs more than 12,000 engineers around the world, making up about a quarter of its workforce. The Bellevue office is a good indication that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) sees AI as something that will play a major role in its business for years, rather than just being another technology trend. Having a dedicated engineering team in a major tech hub should make it easier for Goldman to attract people with experience in AI, cloud computing, and other areas where talent competition is already intense. More engineers focused on AI could also help Goldman automate more of the routine work that takes up employees' time. That could include everything from research and coding to risk management and other internal processes. If Goldman can use AI to help its bankers, traders, and other employees work more efficiently, the firm could potentially get more done without having to increase headcount at the same rate. Over time, that could help keep costs under control and improve margins. Another reason to be positive is that Goldman does not have to figure out how to make money from AI as a standalone business. It can simply use the technology to make the businesses it already has better. AI could help employees analyze information faster, improve client service, automate repetitive tasks, and speed up decision-making. The fact that Goldman is investing in a permanent engineering presence also shows that management appears to be thinking beyond the current AI hype. If the firm can attract good talent and actually put these technologies to work across the business, it could become more efficient and gain an advantage over competitors that are slower to adopt AI. The problem is that all of this will cost money before it starts making money. Hiring highly skilled engineers in the Seattle-area technology market is expensive, and The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) is competing with some of the biggest technology companies for the same people. Salaries and retention costs could therefore add up quickly, while the financial benefits from AI may take several years to become noticeable. There is also no guarantee that Goldman will get a strong return on all of its AI spending. AI technology is changing incredibly quickly, and something the firm invests heavily in today could become outdated sooner than expected. There is also a chance that cheaper third-party AI models could eventually do much of the same work, making some of Goldman's in-house investments less valuable. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) also has to be more careful with AI than a typical technology company. The firm deals with sensitive financial information and operates under strict regulatory requirements. Cybersecurity, privacy, and the risk of AI making incorrect decisions all have to be taken seriously. That means Goldman cannot simply introduce AI tools as quickly as a tech company might. More testing and oversight could slow down adoption and reduce some of the productivity gains the firm is hoping to achieve. Overall, the Bellevue expansion is a positive step for The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS), but the payoff will take time. The new office gives Goldman access to valuable engineering talent and could help the firm make greater use of AI across its existing businesses. If those investments lead to meaningful automation and productivity improvements, they could eventually help Goldman reduce costs and improve profitability. At the same time, investors should not assume that simply spending more on AI will automatically lead to better financial results. Goldman still has to deal with high hiring costs, rapidly changing technology, and strict regulatory requirements. The real test will be whether Goldman can turn its growing AI investment into something investors can actually see in the numbers- higher productivity, lower costs, and stronger profits. Under the agreement, GS Caltex will supply SAF to aircraft operated by DHL Express that refuel in Korea over the next year. The total volume to be supplied to DHL Express is equivalent to 2,000 tons of Neat SAF (100% SAF).

GS Caltex plans to expand SAF production and supply to airlines as market demand grows.
A GS Caltex spokesperson said: “Through the SAF supply agreement with DHL Express, we have taken another step toward expanding the SAF customers,” adding, “We will continue to expand the SAF business and other areas of our biofuel business in response to market demand.”

This shift risks triggering random fluctuations in asset prices, and the crypto market should remain vigilant against cross-asset risks. According to WoofunAI, the low-transparency communication strategy implemented by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is causing deep concern on Wall Street. Jan Hatzius, Chief Economist at Goldman Sachs (GS.US), has explicitly warned that this approach, which sacrifices clarity, will lead to "noise-driven volatility" in the markets. Since assuming office in 2026, Warsh has completely reshaped the Federal Reserve's disclosure framework. His core moves include compressing the length of post-FOMC meeting statements to their shortest level since the Alan Greenspan era and significantly downplaying the status of the dot plot, which had served as the market's "North Star." This shift aims to force the market to focus on real economic fundamentals rather than over-interpreting the central bank's intentions. However, this "speak less, guess more" approach triggered significant turbulence during the Jackson Hole symposium in August 2026. The hawkish tone prompted Goldman Sachs to rapidly raise the probability of a September rate hike to 50%-60%, driving long-term yields higher. Notably, despite severe fluctuations in market sentiment, Hatzius and his team judge that the Federal Reserve will likely hold interest rates steady at its next meeting, based on data indicating that core inflation is expected to remain around 0.2% through the end of August. For traditional financial markets, strategies relying on the dot plot and forward guidance to build models face the risk of becoming ineffective. Traders must re-evaluate trading logic centered on raw economic indicators such as employment data and the CPI, as the premium for correctly interpreting underlying data has risen significantly. A more critical variable is that this uncertainty is transmitting to the crypto market. In recent years, the correlation between Bitcoin and other digital assets with macro liquidity and interest rate expectations has continued to strengthen. A less transparent Federal Reserve implies that interest rate expectations will undergo sudden shifts more frequently, thereby triggering cross-asset volatility that spills over into the crypto market. As the signal-to-noise ratio declines and market noise increases, the challenge for investors has shifted from "guessing the Fed correctly" to "accurately assessing the economy." title: Archisketch's AI 3D interior agent earns top-grade GS certification, eyes public sector - 헤럴드경제
content: Company says it is first in Korea's 3D interior software field to earn the rating Company plans to expand beyond private firms into public, educational institutions Archisketch's AI-powered 3D interior agent, which handles space design and furniture arrangement through natural language commands, has obtained the top grade in South Korea's GS, or Good Software, certification for software quality. The company plans to use the certification as a springboard to expand its business beyond private companies into public institutions and schools. Archisketch, an AI-based 3D interior company, said Friday that its 3D interior agent had received the top-grade GS certification. The company said it is the first in South Korea's 3D interior software field to earn the rating. Archisketch provides 3D space design and consultation solutions used in furniture, interior design, home appliances and retail. Users type in the space and interior style they want in natural language, and the AI agent carries out the related tasks. The tool arranges furniture, products and materials based on an actual space and shows the finished result in 3D. Companies can use this for customer consultations, space planning and design work. The certification's key significance is that it gives Archisketch an objective quality and stability benchmark of the kind companies and public institutions require when adopting business software. The GS certification is a state software quality assurance system that comprehensively tests and evaluates a software's functionality, performance and usability in test environments similar to real operating conditions, based on international standards. The top grade is awarded to products verified using test cases built on those international standards. Products with GS certification can receive institutional support for entering the public procurement market, including designation as a technology product eligible for priority public purchase, registration on the Public Procurement Service's Nara Marketplace, and third-party unit price contracts. Observers say this gives Archisketch a foundation to expand its customer base from private companies into public institutions and schools. In the interior design industry, the spread of cloud-based 3D design and generative AI-powered space design services has made the stability and reliability of enterprise software a key criterion for adoption. Particularly as more agent-based services put AI directly into the consultation and design process, verifying that such tools work reliably in real business settings has become increasingly important. "As 3D interior software becomes widely used in companies' consultation and design work, objective verification of stability and quality, not just functionality, is becoming increasingly important," said Lee Ju-sung, chief executive of Archisketch. "Building on this GS certification, we will strengthen a software foundation that Korean companies and institutions can trust and adopt, and continue to advance our 3D space technology so it can compete in global markets."

title: The ADV Bike With BMW GS Comfort And Italian Character - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Ever since its inception, the boxer GS lineup has attracted thousands of buyers all over the world. The oil-head and hex-head models were quite popular, and the updated wet-head R 1250 GS truly cemented its dominance. The current R 1300 GS and GS Adventure build on that idea, introducing some comprehensive updates in the lineup. These were BMW’s highest-selling bikes last year. However, the base price has risen beyond $20,000, and it breaches $30,000 if you want the full premium bits. That has inevitably opened up the market to rivals, some of which offer a better base package than the GS at a lower starting price. We’re talking about one such bike here, which not only has more oomph than the GS, but it even gets you exotic Italian character. There are a few reasons why the GS lineup has dominated for so long. First and foremost is the reliability. Modern-era boxer-powered GS bikes have always been highly dependable regardless of your use case. Six-digit odometers are common, with very rare major issues. Then, there’s the dollops of performance. Sure, the output isn’t class-leading, but the spread of power is immense, which aids in tractability across terrains. Last but not least is the comfort on offer. BMW’s top-drawer Telelever and Paralever suspension serve as the crown jewels, minimizing dive and unsettling characteristics. That, along with a carefully crafted ergonomic triangle, ensures fatigue is minimal on your tours. A recent addition is the optional Automated Shift Assistant, which means no stress of gear shifts or clutch actuation. As good as all that is, the rivals have truly caught up in recent years. There are worthy alternatives to the GS from all over the world, and even Harley-Davidson whipped up an ADV to rob away sales from the Bavarian company. However, BMW’s biggest headache is from Bologna, offering similar comfort, more power, better technology, and surprisingly, a considerably lower base MSRP. We’re talking about the Ducati Multistrada V4. In base trims, the Multistrada actually offers you more for the money, and this includes comfort. For reference, the base GS has a slim two-up saddle and a puny windscreen, compared to the Multi V4’s visibly larger perch and adjustable windscreen that’s shared with the higher-end variants. In contrast, you need to spend at least $5,000 more if you want the comfier perch on the BMW. Speaking of which, the Multistrada V4 starts at $19,995–an MSRP it has held for a few years, despite a couple of updates in recent times. That makes the Italian ADV $400 cheaper than the base R 1300 GS. That seems like a small difference, but there are some caveats. Firstly, BMW’s official configurator lists the GS’ new base price as $23,795, hinting a large hike for the bike. Secondly, finding a base BMW is like finding a needle in the haystack. We checked several dealers, and the cheapest new R 1300 GS examples we see are equipped with some or the other optional package, taking the total price beyond $24,000. Let’s not forget BMW doesn’t let you pick and choose accessories. Either you get the full $5-6,000 pack, or you don’t get anything. Considering these cases, you’re looking at a net price difference of around $5,000 between the Multi V4 and the GS you actually take home. To make its case stronger, there aren’t any obvious misses for the $19,995 Ducati Multistrada V4. It checks all the boxes you’d expect a premium ADV to, be it in terms of performance, features, or creature comforts. If you feel something is missing, the official accessories take care of that. Let’s dive deeper. If you associate Ducati with Desmo, this is your cue to look away. That’s because the Multistrada V4 boasts a non-Desmo Granturismo engine. This has four cylinders, laid out in a 90-degree V-angle to displace a total of 1,158cc. That helps produce 170 horsepower and 91 pound-feet, where the former is higher but the latter is lower than the twin-cylinder GS. A six-speed transmission sends power to the wheel via a chain final drive. While the absence of desmo valves might feel like a bummer, there are obvious benefits. Firstly, this has allowed Ducati to infuse variable valve timing here. This is said to help spread the power throughout the rev range for extra punch. And having ridden the bike, the system works brilliantly. Next and more important is the service schedule. Ducati’s recommended service interval is a sizable 9,000 miles (or once every two years), while the valve clearance check is at a whopping 37,000 miles. With the V4 engine, Ducati also overhauled the chassis on the Multi V4. Unlike its trellis frame-equipped predecessors, this one has an aluminum monocoque chassis. Ducati says the setup uses learnings from the MotoGP world to ensure sharp handling on the road. When things get rough, the suspension comes into play. Beefy Marzocchi 50 mm USD forks up top and a Sachs monoshock at the rear offer around seven inches of travel. Full adjustability is present to improve versatility, topped with an automatic lowering device at the rear (between 6 and 30 mph). As for wheels and brakes, a 19/17-inch alloy wheel combination is present, each wearing 2x 320 mm and a 280 mm disc, respectively. All that use of aluminum helps Ducati cap the Multistrada V4’s weight at 505 pounds (wet without fuel). That is in the ballpark of its rival, but the seat height is 0.3 inches lower on the Multistrada, thanks to the automatic lowering device. You also get a two-inch longer wheelbase than the GS, which should help with off-road and freeway stability. Being a premium Ducati, there are all the necessary rider aids that improve real-world usability. These are derived from the world of racing, so you know they’ll do their job well. Coming to the package, a six-axis IMU and ride-by-wire allow wheelie control, cornering ABS, and cornering traction control. Ride modes, hill hold, cruise control, and power modes are also present, and so is a two-way quickshifter as standard. Rounding things off is a five-inch TFT display–1.5-inch smaller than the GS.
